content:
I got a bit nerd-sniped this morning. While fixing a merge conflict I found that a newly introduced set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in causing my merge conflict was unnecessary (e.g. it built fine without it.) It was introduced in the 4.33.0-rc1 bump PR #41779 yesterday, this added a new backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types option and 4.5k new set_options for it. It also added 1.5k set_options for the non-.types variant. While sampling a number of these I found that quite a few appeared unnecessary (e.g. deleting them didn't break the build.) I decided to investigate a bit.

On a hunch I found scripts/rm_set_option.py that looks for and deletes set_options and running it found and deleted 3k set_options in mathlib. HOWEVER, I then found that the resulting output didn't build. Indeed, it looks like this script runs automatically once a week and tries to auto-merge the resulting changes after CI, but it has been failing for the past 3 weeks due to build failures: #41136

I then also found that in the 4.33.0-rc1 adaption PR (this is noted by @Paul Reichert in #general > backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency @ 💬) that about ~250 adaption notes were added in the bump PR like the following:

#adaptation_note
/-- `respectTransparency.types true` changes the auto-generated lemmas' signature -/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in

However, scripts/rm_set_option.py is unaware of these so it will happily delete that set_option (and then the resulting PR will be automatically merged once the script is fixed.)

So long story short:

  1. FRO seems to have been too liberal marking theorems with set_option in the bump PR.
  2. The tooling to remove these automatically appears to be broken and I haven't tracked down why.
  3. If it starts working, it will actually silently delete set_options we should probably keep.

In case anyone wants to investigate, running the rm_set_option script takes hours and you can download the output of my run here in case you're planning to take a look. This branch undoes any changes to any files with the adaptation notes. Builds take forever so it's taking me a long time to gather information.

scripts/set_option_utils.py indicates that the tool tries to skip set_option X <value> in -- ... lines. Sounds like it needs to be more conservative (cc @Kim Morrison as the author)

This doesn't seem to be widely known, e.g. #41151 added a

-- The option makes `simps` produce the correct lemmas
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Restricting scalars along the identity is isomorphic to the identity. -/
@[simps!]
def restrictScalarsId' {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (f : R →+* R) (hf : f = .id R) :

which then gets deleted by the script. (though maybe it should also be updated to .types since it matches that pattern?)
(I actually suspect that that PR may be why the CI started failing but I can't confirm that yet)

Actually I now suspect it was #36572 that caused CI to break, via this addition to IsLimit.lean. However, this was given an adaptation note in the 4.33.0-rc1 bump PR (though the change from #41151 was not)

-- The `set_option` is needed to make reassoc generate the right theorem
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[to_dual (attr := reassoc (attr := simp)) (reorder := c hd d) ι_map]
theorem map_π {F G : J ⥤ C} (c : Cone F) {d : Cone G} (hd : IsLimit d) (α : F ⟶ G) (j : J) :

Actually, the adaptation note may be kind of bad, the change is

--- The `set_option` is needed to make reassoc generate the right theorem
-set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
+#adaptation_note
+/-- `respectTransparency.types true` changes the auto-generated lemmas' signature -/
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in
Thanks for digging into this! I would be happy to review / merge fixes to the rm_set_option script / workflow.
(bad in the sense that it's not clear if we ALSO need it for reassoc)

Note that some adaptation notes were also added of the form so the eventual fix should also be able to handle them.

#adaptation_note
/--
`mapIsoWhiskerRight`'s `simps` theorems were formulated in simp normal form under
`respectTransparency.types true`. We use `respectTransparency.types false` here because these
lemmas fail to match without this annotation.
Suggested way forward: Decide what the correct signatures of the `mapIsoWhiskerRight` lemmas
are, then update this proof accordingly.
-/
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

Thanks for digging into this! I would be happy to review / merge fixes to the rm_set_option script / workflow.

I've already spent too much time on this so I am going to leave the script change (looking for #adaptation_notes and -- comments) to someone else. But I would like to finish understanding the root causes.

There is a single change I need to make to make Mathlib finish building with set_options deleted, I need to add

--- a/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean
+++ b/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean
@@ -140,6 +140,7 @@ lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_fst (Y : Over X) :
     (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.fst _ (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 _ :=
   limit.lift_π _ _

+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in
 @[reassoc (attr := simp)]
 lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
     (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (𝟙 X) = Y.hom :=

so that isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_isIntegral_tensorObj_of_isAlgClosed builds downstream (otherwise a simp fails on the second to last line). I am sure someone knows what this has to do with respectTransparency but I don't. Anyways, it seems bad that rm_set_option would delete this line and change the underlying theory without realizing it.

I think the only things left to do are 1) figure out the root cause of why we need the set_option above, 2) someone actually patching the script, and 3) @Jovan Gerbscheid maybe you want to add your reassoc comment back from above? (also maybe this is related to my issue above so you can offer some advice? :)

Thanks for noticing that these set_options are being auto-removed by rm_set_option.py; I wasn't aware that there are special conventions for preventing pruning by an automated script! Regarding the superfluous options, this was a change I worked on for a long time; I believe some fixes I added later might have resolved some of the initial problems, making some options obsolete.

Which of the set_options do you mean when you say you want to know why it is needed? Update: Oh, you mean rightUnitor_inv_left_snd? I can take a look.

The reason is the same as for the options with an adaptation note, and this one should probably also have gotten such a note. reassoc internally uses simp to simplify its LHS. But if the codomain of the first functor and the domain of the second functor are not definitionally equal at implicit transparency, then comp_assoc cannot be applied by simp, and so the lemma gets the wrong signature.

We can confirm with set_option trace.Meta.Tactic.simp true:

[Meta.Tactic.simp.unify] Category.assoc:1000, failed to unify
      (?f ≫ ?g) ≫ ?h
    with
      (Hom.left (ρ_ Y).inv ≫ pullback.snd Y.hom (𝟙 X)) ≫ h

In this case, unifying the codomain of the first and domain of the second functor means solving [implicit] (Y ⊗ 𝟙_ (Over X)).left ⟶ X =?= Limits.pullback Y.hom (𝟙 X) ⟶ X.

Enabling a linter helps to diagnose:

set_option linter.tacticCheckInstances true in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false in
@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
lemma rightUnitor_inv_left_snd (Y : Over X) :
    (ρ_ Y).inv.left ≫ pullback.snd _ (𝟙 X) = Y.hom :=
  limit.lift_π _ _

Indeed, the linter warns about the lemma generated by reassoc:

generated lemma CategoryTheory.Over.rightUnitor_inv_left_snd_assoc is not type-correct at `.implicit` transparency; consider marking some of the following as `@[implicit_reducible]`:
  getLimitCone
  Quiver.Hom
  tensorUnit
  pullbackConeEquivBinaryFan
  CategoryStruct.id
  limit.cone

Note: This linter can be disabled with `set_option linter.tacticCheckInstances false`

In this case, the definitions that need to be implicit-reducible for this to work turn out to be pullbackConeEquivBinaryFan and limit.cone, because these need to be unfolded in order to compute the domain and codomain objects mentioned above.

OK, I'm not qualified to propose what the right change maybe for the category theory library, but I opened #41837 to add that adaptation note so that it won't be casually deleted in the future. Then the only thing remaining is to update the script and this workflow will start working again. Thanks for looking into it!

So I had a look at fixing this again. I updated the rm_set_option.py script and ran it over night and the resulting build almost succeeded, except it failed in a file that just landed yesterday due to a lemma in Over.lean again. There are a number of other @[reassoc] lemmas that were having their set_option removed and I was able to verify that every _assoc lemma type signature in that file changes if it has set_option removed. Claude wrote a 10 line script that pretty prints all decls with _assoc in the namespace after importing Mathlib and a found another couple of differences after rm_set_option ran. This makes me a bit nervous because probably there other are cases silently hanging around that may get deleted in the future without anyone noticing (or perhaps this CI job will break again and no one will notice that).

Interestingly, at least one of these changes occurs after deleting a set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in that was added in the original 4.29.0-rc1 bump so this has silently been a problem this entire time.
#41996 adds more #adaptation_notes to that one file.
#41997 updates rm_set_option.py to ignore preceding comments/adaptation notes
Question for our metaprogramming experts: Is there something we should modify in reassoc here to keep more of these from popping up? (Is someone already looking at this?)

Now that we have implicit_reducible separate from instance_reducible, I would hope that we can work on fixing these cases where reassoc fails, rather than needing the set_options.

Either way, it would probably be possible to have reassoc always try with and without respectTransparency, and if they are different then give a linter warning. I'm not sure though if this linter would give false positives.

I had a go at removing some set_option by using implicit_reducible in category theory in #42161. This removes a couple hundred set_option, and also reduces the number of set_option that are needed to make reassoc generate correct theorems.

Right now I'm looking at somewhat difficult-to-remove annotations in UniversalFactorizationRing and MFDeriv.Basic. Just in case somebody is considering them, don't waste time on these right now. I need to diagnose what's going on there and perhaps a toolchain-level fix is needed for those.

In MFDeriv.Basic, there are definitely some ugly defeq abuses, especially in the definition of the derivative (I know because I wrote them :-). The fix should probably be at the Mathlib level, not in core: the level of defeq abuse here is too much. The correct fix would probably be to insert some identification between the tangent space and the model space, as a continuous linear equiv, and compose with these to avoid the abuses. You said that we shouldn't waste time on thse, so I won't implement that, but if you think a proper fix may help here don't hesitate to ask!
(Tangentially relevant: #42038 and #42034 fix some defeq abuse in differential geometry, but unrelated to that file.)
docs#NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace may be the identification you're looking for, or at least related.

Okay, fixing the Lean-internal problems and making the file more robust seems like a good compromise ;)

I'll try my hand for now and then give you an update. (If you're able to easily fix some of the annotations, I'd be very happy too, I just want to avoid that you end up dealing with weird Lean internals.)

Michael Rothgang said:

(Tangentially relevant: #42038 and #42034 fix some defeq abuse in differential geometry, but unrelated to that file.)

Great!

Michael Rothgang said:

docs#NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace may be the identification you're looking for, or at least related.

I'll take a look, thanks.

Probably you're already aware; just in case you're not: there is a Lean core bug affecting differential geometry, that I talked through with Julia (in Lisbon, in May). She had a fix for that. I'm not sure that the precise status of that is. Enabling backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types was a prerequisite for that (which is true in mathlib now).
Oh yes, I think that's related to lean4#13846. Getting that ready is on my to-do list at least, but not done yet unfortunately.

Okay, MFDeriv's problems vanish after making the type alias TangentSpace implicit-reducible (reasonable, I think: type aliases should almost never be semireducible).

Regarding UniversalFactorizationRing, there is a bug that makes the comparison HMul.hMul x y =?= Mul.mul x y at implicit transparency fail during instance search if the Mul instance is a metavariable; Lean fails to reduce the LHS there. I have a proof of concept for a fix, but it requires a bit more thought.

Okay, MFDeriv's problems vanish after making the type alias TangentSpace implicit-reducible (reasonable, I think: type aliases should almost never be semireducible).

I am not so sure if this is a good idea. Mathematically, tangent spaces at different points are different objects - being able to identify them all over without any warning is not great. While this identification is used in a number of places; I'd like to see how bad making this identification explicit instead (#42193, started by Sébastien) is in practice. This identification will clearly be needed in foundational files; I'm not convinced yet it will show up a lot later (and if so, then that's a better fix).

(Also, the bug I reported to Julia was about Lean confusing an instance on a TangentSpace with an instance on the underlying normed space E. So, this might also lead to other formalization issues. The code is question is close to getting merged into mathlib, but will probably take a day or two.)

I think I ran into issues with the TangentSpace identification in a few places, but if there's a way to avoid it, I'm all for it. :)
But if you don't want it implicit_reducible, then could we consider making TangentSpace irreducible? Semireducible types lead to really bad behavior.
Also note that making TangentSpace implicit-reducible doesn't affect type class search.

Paul Reichert said:

making the type alias TangentSpace implicit-reducible (reasonable, I think: type aliases should almost never be semireducible).

If I recall correctly, TangentSpace was part of the issue half a year ago (lean#9077) which prompted the FRO to implement the respectTransparency feature. The problem was that this type synonym was being unfolded in some unification where it should not be unfolded.

Your claim that making type aliases implicit-reducible will fix our problems, makes me feel uneasy, because it seems like we are reverting all of the work from the last half a year and we will be back where we started.
Am I saying this right @Sébastien Gouëzel?

The lean4#9077 issue is what I'm currently fixing; my claim that "it doesn't affect instance search" was meant as "after my fix, it doesn't affect instance search". So after my fix, one shouldn't think of implicit_reducible as having the lean4#9077 problem.

There's also a wholly different reason for respectTransparency, which is the ability to control the cost of unfolding, making Lean more scalable. If there are scalability issues with the unfolding of TangentSpace, then that would be interesting to know.
Are you mostly worried about instance search or something else?

Yes I am worried about implicit_reducible types having the lean#9077 problem. How are you planning to fix this?

My understanding was that lean#9077 is caused by the fact that instances are being unified implicitly. And obviously, an implicit_reducible type does not stop this implicit unification.
Are you planning to, when unifying instances in implicit transparency, also unify their types in instances` transparency?
Essentially yes; see the thread #mathlib4 > Fixing lean#9077 for a more detailed explanation of the plan.

Also note that making TangentSpace implicit-reducible doesn't affect type class search.

I know, and this is very good. (Making TangentSpace instance_reducible is wrong, also mathematically. docs#TangentSpace is not a normed space, and intentionally so (there is no canonical norm on it). Making it instance-reducible would find the wrong norm on it.)

On a positive note: this split into implicit and instance reducible is also great for differential geometry. I didn't think about this back when this was discussed, so let me mention it now :-)
For instance, docs#ModelProd and docs#ModelPi could never be instance reducible, but they can be implicit reducible just fine.

But if you don't want it implicit_reducible, then could we consider making TangentSpace irreducible? Semireducible types lead to really bad behavior.

Good question! I'll have to think about it. @Sébastien Gouëzel What do you think?
I just tried activating another round of scripts/rm_set_option.py here. Hopefully it will manage to remove the set_options without causing build failures this time.
That build failure is in the same file that was the cause for #41996. I hope that once that lands it will run successfully.
Ah you're right. I've taken a look at your PR #41996, and I've instead made #42267, which instead removes those backwards options altogether, by using some more implicit_reducible in category theory.
For reference, #41136 is the auto-generated PR that tries to remove unnecessary set_option

Note that in #41136 there are some linter warnings from the unused simp arguments linter. The linter fires on these declarations only after removing the backward option. I've created #42270 that addresses these cases.
